question: Will Russia enter Moskovka by July 31?
rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Moskovka, Kharkiv Oblast, (49.729536° N, 37.568362° E) between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

The boundaries of the municipality are those shown under the “Ukrainian Settlements” layer on the ISW map.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be consider

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Gerasimov also reiterated his claim that Russian forces are advancing west from Kupyansk towards Shevchenkove, though Russian forces have not yet seized Kupyansk and do not currently have any consolidated advances in the town besides limited infiltration zones. A source reporting on the Russian Northern Grouping of Forces (GoF) acknowledged on July 18 that Ukrainian forces again control Kupyansk-Vuzlovyi (just south of Kupyansk) after Russian forces previously conducted infiltration missions to the settlement.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Russian forces continued offensive operations in the Kupyansk direction on July 16 and 17 but did not advance. A spokesperson for a Ukrainian brigade operating in the Kupyansk direction reported on July 17 that Russian forces are relying on infiltration tactics and launching KAB glide bomb and drone strikes against Ukrainian forces and civilian targets in an attempt to undermine Ukrainian rear positions.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War / AEI Critical Threats Project
evidence.excerpt: Russian forces continued limited offensive operations in the Kupyansk and Borova directions on July 15 and 16 but did not advance. Geolocated footage published on July 16 shows Russian forces striking a Ukrainian position west of Holubivka (just north of Kupyansk), an area where Russian sources previously claimed that Russian forces maintained positions.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Geolocated footage published on July 14 shows Ukrainian forces striking a Russian position in central Kupyansk after what ISW assesses was a Russian infiltration mission. Mashovets acknowledged that small Russian infiltration groups are in Kupyansk but emphasized that Russian forces do not exercise physical control over the areas where they operate. Mashovets reported that Russian numerical superiority, Russian use of foliage for concealment, and the dense urban environment are slowly deteriorating the Ukrainian tactical situation near the Russian foothold in the Kupyansk direction.

Russian troops are trying to expand their presence along the state border of Ukraine, using the tactics of small assault groups and seeking new areas for penetration. The situation remains most tense in the Lyman and Kupiansk directions. This was reported by Viktor Trehubov, spokesperson of the Joint Forces Group, during a telethon broadcast, as reported by UNN.
